aboutGame.title: What is Rockbeasts?
paragraphs: Rockbeasts is a band-management music RPG where you steer a crew of beastly musicians from scruffy small-venue gigs toward rock stardom. Instead of shredding solos yourself, you run the business and the relationships that make the shows possible: booking gigs, reading crowds, calming egos, and deciding when to push a band past its breaking point.

Every week you balance four pools of resources — cash, energy, hype, and cohesion — while songwriting and setlist choices decide how a show lands. The narrative unfolds between performances, in van rides and backstage arguments, so the decisions you make offstage shape who the band becomes on it.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about Rockbeasts.

items.question: What is Rockbeasts?
items.answer: Rockbeasts is a band-management music RPG where you steer a crew of beastly musicians from small venues to rock stardom. You balance money, energy, chemistry, and morale while writing songs and playing live shows.

items.question: Is Rockbeasts a rhythm game?
items.answer: No. Rockbeasts is a management RPG: you plan tours, build setlists, and make live calls while the show unfolds instead of matching notes to a beat map.

items.question: What should beginners focus on first in Rockbeasts?
items.answer: Rockbeasts rewards patience. Protect cohesion and morale, keep a cash buffer, write before you book, and never accept every paying gig that comes your way.

items.question: Which platforms is Rockbeasts on?
items.answer: Rockbeasts targets PC storefronts plus console platforms. Check the official store listing for your region to confirm availability and system requirements.

items.question: Does Rockbeasts have a demo?
items.answer: Yes. The Rockbeasts demo offers a self-contained slice with the opening tutorial, early areas, and a taste of the progression systems before the full release.

items.question: How do Rockbeasts choices affect the story?
items.answer: Dialogue, roster, and route decisions set flags that ripple forward across the tour, shaping relationships, reputation, and which endings your band can reach.
